raw_case_text:
A 54-year-old previously healthy female presented to the hospital with intermittent low-grade fever for two months with a mild dry cough. There was no associated pleuritic chest pain, shortness of breath, or hemoptysis. Accompanying anorexia and weight loss were pronounced. She gave a recent history of being investigated for right side loin pain, where she was managed as right renal calculus, which was evident with the ultrasound scan. But she did not have urinary symptoms or hematuria. Examination revealed a female who looked ill. She was averagely built but claimed that she has been overweight previously. She was afebrile and had mild pallor. There were no enlarged lymph glands. Respiratory system was clinically normal without pleural effusions or added sounds. She had regular pulse rate of 72 bpm and blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg. She had no hepatosplenomegaly or ballotable loin masses. She gave a history of being treated by several doctors with antibiotics for a possible infection.
Her complete blood count revealed normal white cell and platelet count. Her hemoglobin was 9.4 x 103/muL with a normochromic normocytic anemia. Her inflammatory markers were significantly elevated with an ESR of 130 in the first hour and CRP of 124 u/l. Blood, urine, and sputum for pyogenic, mycobacterial, and fungal cultures were negative repeatedly, while the chest radiograph showed multiple bilateral opacities with small nodular lesions over all three zones of both lungs (Figure 1). Mantoux test revealed a wheal of 12 mm and the serology and cultures for melioidosis were negative. She had normal renal function tests with normal urine analysis. The liver functions revealed mildly elevated SGOT and SGPT (80/68 u/l) with markedly elevated ALP (417 U/L) and GGT (592 U/L). The total bilirubin was normal. Ultrasound scan of the abdomen was done twice and did not reveal a significant abnormality.
We empirically treated her for possible chest infection with intravenous antibiotics (ceftazidime) for two weeks. But neither the fever nor the inflammatory markers showed any response and the lung opacities were persistent. Next, we performed a contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) of chest and abdomen. The CECT revealed a renal cell carcinoma of the right kidney (Figure 2) with multiple pulmonary metastasis (Figure 3).
She was transferred for oncology care and was treated with oral Sunitinib, a multitargeted receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor, in the hope of subsequent nephrectomy. With treatment, the hepatic abnormalities resolved.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old previously healthy woman presented with a 2-month history of intermittent low-grade fever, mild dry cough, pronounced anorexia, and weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced 2 months of intermittent low-grade fever, mild dry cough, marked anorexia, and weight loss. She had previously received multiple courses of oral antibiotics from several physicians for a presumed infection without improvement, and had recently been evaluated for right-sided loin pain and managed for a right renal calculus noted on ultrasound.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy; recently evaluated and managed for a right renal calculus following right loin pain.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for intermittent low-grade fever, mild dry cough, pronounced anorexia, weight loss, and recent right loin pain. Negative for pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis, dysuria, or hematuria.

objective.physical_examination: Ill-appearing, averagely built female (reporting prior overweight status), afebrile on admission, with mild pallor, regular pulse rate of 72 bpm, and blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg. No palpable lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or ballotable loin masses were present, and respiratory examination was normal without pleural effusions or adventitious sounds.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count showed normocytic normochromic anemia with hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL (reported as 9.4 x 10^3/muL in text) and normal WBC and platelet counts. Inflammatory markers were markedly elevated with ESR 130 mm in the 1st hour and CRP 124 U/L. Renal function tests, urinalysis, and total bilirubin were normal, while liver enzymes were elevated: SGOT (AST) 80 U/L, SGPT (ALT) 68 U/L, ALP 417 U/L, and GGT 592 U/L. Serial blood, urine, and sputum cultures for pyogenic bacteria, mycobacteria, and fungi were negative. Mantoux test showed a 12 mm wheal, and melioidosis serology and cultures were negative. Chest radiograph showed multiple bilateral small nodular opacities across all three lung zones, and two abdominal ultrasound scans reported no significant abnormality.
objective.advanced_workup: Following failure of a 2-week empiric course of intravenous ceftazidime, contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) of the chest and abdomen was performed and revealed a right renal cell carcinoma with multiple bilateral pulmonary metastases.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Metastatic right renal cell carcinoma with multiple bilateral pulmonary metastases and paraneoplastic hepatopathy (Stauffer syndrome), initially mimicking disseminated pulmonary tuberculosis or melioidosis (both ruled out by negative cultures, negative melioidosis serology, and lack of response to 2 weeks of empiric IV ceftazidime). Management and outcome: Transferred to oncology care and initiated on oral sunitinib (a multitargeted receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor) with a plan for subsequent cytoreductive nephrectomy; on sunitinib therapy, her hepatic enzyme abnormalities resolved.
